Series::mm¶

Back to SeriesLinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signature¶

Series::mm(const Series& other) const -> Series
Series::linearalg.mm(const Series& other) const -> Series
Series::linearalg(const Series& other).mm() const -> Series

What It Does¶

mm() performs matrix-matrix multiplication and requires both operands to be two-dimensional.

If the left matrix has shape [m, k] and the right matrix has shape [k, n], the result has shape [m, n]. Each output entry is the inner product of one left row and one right column.

Choose mm() when two-dimensionality is part of your program’s contract. If a vector or batched matrix arrives accidentally, the method rejects it at the call site instead of changing the meaning or rank of the result.

Parameter¶

other (const Series&) The right-hand matrix. It must be two-dimensional, share dtype and platform with the left matrix, and have a first dimension equal to the left matrix’s second dimension.

Returns¶

Series A new two-dimensional matrix with shape [left.size(0), other.size(1)].

Gradient¶

mm() uses the ordinary matrix-product reverse rule. For C = A B and incoming sensitivity G:

dL/dA = G B^T
dL/dB = A^T G

Both operands can be tracked. Neither operand is mutated.

Examples¶

Example 1. The direct-peer and peer-bound accessor spellings are equivalent.

auto left = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, 2.0},
    {3.0, 4.0},
});
auto right = pluss::make_series({
    {2.0, 0.0},
    {1.0, 2.0},
});

std::cout << "peer_argument=" << left.linearalg.mm(right) << "\n";
std::cout << "peer_bound=" << left.linearalg(right).mm() << "\n";

The first output column is [1*2 + 2*1, 3*2 + 4*1] = [4, 10]. The second is [4, 8].

Output¶

peer_argument=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[4, 4],
  [10, 8]]
peer_bound=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[4, 4],
  [10, 8]]

Example 2. A vector is not a matrix and is rejected.

try {
  auto matrix = pluss::make_series({
      {1.0, 2.0},
      {3.0, 4.0},
  });
  std::cout << matrix.linearalg.mm(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0})) << "\n";
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::cout << e.what() << "\n";
}

Output¶

mm: expected two 2D Series

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Both operands must be rank 2. Use matmul() for vectors or batches.

  • The inner dimensions must match.

  • Dtypes and platforms must match.

  • mm() does not perform elementwise multiplication.

Summary¶

Use mm() when the operation is specifically matrix by matrix and rank drift should fail early.

See Also¶

  • Series::matmul: rank-polymorphic multiplication.

  • Series::mv: matrix-vector multiplication.

  • Series::mul: elementwise multiplication.
